name: YNAB
tagline: Personal budgeting app built around zero-based budgeting and habit formation

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; monthly plan listed at $14.99/month and annual at $109/year.

tiers.name: YNAB
tiers.limits: All features; share one subscription with up to 5 other people (6 total)
tiers.notes: 34-day trial when signing up directly; annual is $109/year.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 34-day free trial; up to 6 people can share one paid subscription
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual ($109/year); taxes extra where applicable
pricing.hiddenCosts: Third-party app stores may require a card for the trial and can use different billing terms.

verdictSummary: A zero-based budget app with accounts, categories, envelopes, and reports is very buildable; bank sync and habit coaching are the main paid value.
coreLoopDIY: Build account/category tables, assign dollars to categories, import transactions, reconcile balances, and show budget reports.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the method and mobile/bank-sync habit are easier to follow than a spreadsheet.

priorArt.name: Actual Budget
priorArt.desc: Open-source local-first budgeting app and one of the strongest YNAB alternatives.

alternatives.name: Actual Budget
alternatives.desc: Envelope budgeting, imports and rules on your own disk; bank sync is optional, not the landlord.

facts.install: Native desktop app for local-only use, or the official Docker/Node server for browser access and device sync
facts.dataFormat: Each client works from a local SQLite budget; the server keeps account metadata plus budget blobs under its data directory, and optional end-to-end encryption covers budget contents but not bank-sync tokens.
facts.gapVsPaid: Actual reproduces envelope budgeting well but lacks YNAB's polished mobile coaching, educational method, support community, and turnkey bank connections.

alternatives.name: OpenBudgeteer
alternatives.desc: YNAB-style buckets in a Docker box; bank sync and habit coaching did not make the container.

facts.dataFormat: Budget buckets, accounts, transactions, users, and settings live in the deployment's MariaDB database, with Redis used by the application stack.
facts.gapVsPaid: OpenBudgeteer supplies buckets but not YNAB's native apps, live bank connections, habit-building guidance, polished reports, and managed cross-device reliability.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a multi-container deployment with MariaDB, Redis, persistent volumes, secrets, TLS, backups, and no built-in live bank connection.

alternatives.name: Aspire Budgeting
alternatives.desc: A polished zero-based budget living in Google Sheets; CSV imports and auto-categorization are the paid shortcut.

facts.install: Make a copy of the free Google Sheets template; the optional Workspace add-on can be installed separately
facts.dataFormat: The budget is an ordinary Google Sheet in the user's Google Drive; Aspire says the add-on does not require a separate Aspire account, while Google stores and processes the sheet.
facts.gapVsPaid: Aspire is a spreadsheet rather than a purpose-built app and gives up YNAB's mobile entry, live bank sync, automatic categorization, guided workflow, and interaction polish.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Cashew
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The store app kept moving while meaningful public source work stopped in 2024; a README edit in March 2026 is not maintenance.

notes: One of the best consumer-subscription yes pages due strong prior art.
prompt:
Build me a zero-based budgeting app to replace YNAB. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered, binds to
  localhost only.
- Accounts (checking, credit card, cash) and categories in groups. Every dollar of
  inflow gets assigned; a To Be Budgeted header shows what is unassigned and goes
  red if I over-assign.
- Budget view: month grid of category · assigned · activity · available, with
  available balances rolling over month to month.
- Transactions: a fast keyboard entry form plus CSV import from bank exports, with
  payee-to-category memory so repeat payees auto-fill.
- Reconcile flow: enter the real bank balance, the app shows the difference and
  marks matched transactions cleared.
- Reports: spending by category per month and net worth over time, drawn with
  Chart.js.
- Nightly copy of budget.db to backups/budget-YYYY-MM-DD.db, keep 30.
- No accounts, no telemetry, and no bank credentials anywhere; CSV import is the
  only way money data enters.
- Out of scope: automatic bank sync, mobile apps, and shared budgets. A weekly CSV
  import is the habit that replaces sync.
- README: how to map my bank's CSV columns on first import.
